platform_notes: The DejaPayPro D1 is an Android 11 register that runs Dejavoo's DejaPayPro POS software with the DeNovo web back office, takes cards on its own chip/NFC readers or a paired Dejavoo terminal over SPIn, and processes through the iPOSpays gateway. The iPOSpays Virtual Terminal (CloudPOS) is the browser portal at ipospays.com where merchants key payments or push them to a Dejavoo pinpad; terminal settings live in the portal's S.T.E.A.M parameters per TPN. iPOSpays is the gateway behind every Dejavoo terminal, so its response-code tables (gateway codes, S.A.F.E risk declines and the host codes passed through from TSYS, Fiserv, Worldpay, Elavon, EPX, RS2 and BridgePay) apply to all of them.

A stop payment order shall remain in effect until the earliest of the following occurs: a lapse of six months from the date of the stop payment order, payment of the debit entry has been stopped, or the Receiver withdraws the stop payment order.

What to Do: Contact your customer and resolve any issues that caused the transaction to be stopped.
You can re-enter the returned transaction again with proper authorization from your customer. You can also ask your customer for a different form of payment.

entries.title: R10: Customer Advises Not Authorized; Item Is Ineligible, Notice Not Provided, Signatures Not Genuine, or Item Altered (adjustment entries) (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: For entries to Consumer Accounts that are not PPD debit entries constituting notice of presentment or PPD Accounts Receivable Truncated Check Debit Entries in accordance with Article Two, subsection 2.1.4(2), the RDFI has been notified by its customer, the Receiver, that the Originator of a given transaction has not been authorized to debit his account.

What to Do: The Receiver may request immediate credit from the RDFI for an unauthorized debit. The request must be made in writing within fifteen (15) days after the RDFI sends or makes available to the Receiver information pertaining to that debit entry.

Immediately suspend any recurring payment schedules entered for this bank account. This will prevent additional transactions from being returned while you address the issue with your customer. Then contact your customer and resolve any issues that caused the transaction to be disputed or the schedule to be cancelled.
You can ask the customer for a different form of payment, or ask to debit a different bank account.
If you need to debit the same bank account, instruct your customer to call the bank and remove the block on transactions.

Unfortunately, there is no dispute resolution available to you within the ACH Network. If your customer continues to claim the transaction was not authorized, but you have proof that it was properly authorized, you will need to sue your customer in Small Claims Court to collect. If this action is taken, please contact Vericheck.

entries.title: R11: Customer Advises Entry Not Within the Authorization Terms (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: Used by the RDFI to return an entry for which the Originator and Receiver have a relationship, and an authorization to debit exists, but there is an error or defect in the payment such that the entry does not conform to the terms of the authorization (i.e., "an incorrect amount," "payment was debited earlier than authorized"). For ARC, BOC or POP errors with the original source document and errors may exist (i.e., "document is ineligible", "notice was not provided to Receiver", "amount was not accurate per the source document").

What to Do: The originator can correct the underlying error, e.g. correct the amount, the date, and resubmit the corrected entry as a new entry. No new authorization is needed from the customer. The new corrected entry must be submitted and originated within 60 days of the Settlement Date of the R11 Return Entry.
If a correction and new entry submission is not possible, the resolution would be similar to receiving a return with the R10 code. See "What to do" for R10 code.

entries.title: R12: Branch Sold to Another DFI (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: A financial institution may continue to receive entries destined for an account at a branch that has been sold to another financial institution. Because the RDFI no longer maintains the account and is unable to post the entry, it should return the entry to the ODFI.
What to Do: Obtain new Routing Number and Bank Account Number information, then enter a NEW transaction using the updated account numbers.
If the transaction was part of a recurring payment schedule, be sure to update the schedule to use the new bank account.

entries.title: R23: Credit Entry Refused by Receiver (Vericheck ACH return code)

entries.title: The operation has timed out (SPIn message between the register and the terminal)
steps: A request was sent to a terminal, but the terminal did not provide a response at a proper time. Probably the terminal lost a connection, was switched off, a discharged battery, some bug on a terminal, a terminal not in the IDLE screen and busy by some process e.g. a terminal menu is open and a transaction not in focus.

Possible that the terminal will respond to this transaction after a timeout event, a transaction will be performed and approved on a host side and added to a settlement report. But SPIn Proxy cannot guarantee a delivery on this POS request and a timeout is the best response in this case.
Default timeout 120 seconds.
Check a terminal whether it works or not and be sure that terminal is on the SPIn mode screen and online.
Do Status request to check transaction Status.
Repeat the transaction with the same parameters if the transaction was already performed you will get an error “Duplicated ReferenceID”.
Continue to perform transactions.

entries.title: Add items to a customer's cart in DejaPayPro
steps: Tap the department the item is in.

To change a quantity, highlight the item and tap +1 or -1.
To type a quantity, tap MANUAL, enter the new quantity and tap ENTER.
To add a note to an item, highlight it, tap COMMENT, type the comment and press SAVE.
Continue until all items are in the cart.

entries.title: Apply a discount to the cart in DejaPayPro
steps: Tap the DISCOUNT button.
Tap the discount amount you want for the cart.
Tap DOUBLE DISCOUNT to double it, or NORMAL for a normal discount.

entries.title: Take a cash payment in DejaPayPro

Tap CLOSE to finish. It also closes by itself after several seconds.

Have the customer enter their PIN on the terminal and press OK.
Tap CLOSE to finish.

entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

If tip adjust is not available, ask support to check the Tips setting on the TPN.
entries.quote: It allows merchants do to tip adjust from the portal.
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: Manual versus automatic settlement on iPOSpays terminals
steps: With Manual Settlement the merchant must settle from the POS device.
With Automatic Settlement a mode and time are chosen in the TPN parameters.
If the automatic settlement is POS initiated, a print receipt choice is also set.
To change the mode or time, ask support to edit the TPN's Settlement parameters.
entries.quote: Merchant must do the settlement activity from a POS device.
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Transaction types, entry modes and card types are switched on per TPN
steps: The TPN's Transaction section selects the allowed transaction types, card entry modes and card types.
AVS, Signature Line, Cash Back, Pin Prompt and PinBypass Debit are also enabled there.
If a transaction type or card type is not offered, ask support to check the TPN's Transaction parameters.
entries.quote: Tx Type (Transaction Type) – Select the required transaction types, card entry
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: A pinpad paired to a Dejavoo terminal uses the same TPN as the main terminal
steps: The same TPN number must be entered on both the Slave (pinpad) and Master devices.
The Master device's parameters are then assigned to the Slave automatically.
entries.quote: Note: Same TPN Number should be entered on both Slave & Master devices.
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: Consumer choice fee setting
steps: With Consumer choice selected in the TPN's Fee section, customers can choose whether to pay with cash or card.
The fee percentage is entered in the same place.
Changes to the fee are made in the TPN parameters by support.
entries.quote: Consumer choice: Consumers can choose whether to pay with cash or card
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: D1 accepts chip, tap and mobile wallets
steps: The D1 has Smart IC (chip) and NFC readers with EMV certification.
It is compatible with Apple Pay, Google Wallet and Samsung Pay.
entries.quote: Compatible with Apple Pay, Google Wallet, and Samsung Pay

entries.title: Software the D1 runs
steps: Dejavoo says the D1 runs DejaPayPro and connects to DeNovo for business management.
Its compatible software is listed as iPOSpays and SPIn.
It works with Dejavoo PIN pads as an add-on.
entries.quote: Runs DejaPayPro and connects to DeNovo for full business management

entries.title: DvPay app corrupted or obsolete on a Dejavoo Android terminal (reinstall)
steps: This is a technician procedure that uses the administrator password.
In settings go to About POS, POS Configuration, Administrator Login and log in.
From the apps list uninstall DVPAY/AURA. Force Stop the Market app and Clear Data in its Storage.
Open Market, let it update, then install DVPay.
Install the TPN again through utility, Software Download.
entries.quote: locate DVPAY/AURA and uninstall. Look for Market and Force Stop
entries.note: Tier 2 (PayCompass); written for Dejavoo Android terminals running DvPay and does not name the D1. The article gives admin password 01062009 and utility password 1234

entries.title: Factory reset a Dejavoo Android terminal
steps: This is a technician procedure that uses the administrator password.
Go to settings, About POS, POS Configuration and log in as ADMIN.
Go back to Android settings, Back up and Factory Reset, and proceed with the factory reset.
entries.quote: go to settings then go to About POS then go to POS Configuration then login as ADMIN (01062009 OR 99999999)
entries.note: Tier 2 (PayCompass); written for Dejavoo Android terminals running DvPay and does not name the D1

entries.title: iPOSpays portal users and permissions
steps: Unlimited users can be added to iPOSpays.
Role based permission settings are available.
entries.quote: Number of users & cost per user: Unlimited users can be added
entries.note: Tier 2 (PayCompass)

entries.title: When iPOSpays creates a customer record after a payment
steps: A new customer record is created when payment is made by invoice, payment link or itemized billing.
The Quick pay feature does not create a customer profile.
entries.quote: New customer profiles are not generated with "Quick pay" feature.
entries.note: Tier 2 (PayCompass)

entries.title: iPOSpays stores cards as tokens
steps: Card vaulting is available, but only as a token, not raw card data.
Multiple payment methods per customer are kept through tokenization and the My Customers module.
entries.quote: Card authorization with card vaulting: Yes, but only as a token not raw card data.
entries.note: Tier 2 (PayCompass)

entries.title: Payment methods and features in iPOSpays
steps: iPOSpays accepts cash, credit/debit and ACH.
It offers invoicing, recurring billing, payment pages, scheduled payments, QR code payments and text to pay.
It does not send automated payment reminders to customers.
entries.quote: Send automated reminder to customers for payment: No
entries.note: Tier 2 (PayCompass)

entries.title: First Data North: which Dejavoo devices are supported
steps: On First Data North, the QD series is not supported.
iPOSGo! is not supported.
The Z and P series are supported.
entries.quote: First Data North NO QD series NO iPOSGo! YES Z & P series
entries.note: Tier 2 (PayCompass). applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: Dejavoo 2024 advisory: terminals processing without the P2PE key
steps: In 2024 Dejavoo found some gateway terminals with Point to Point Encryption disabled or not activated because of incorrect TPN parameters.
Most were fixed automatically through Auto Download and Auto RKL.
A few terminals need manual intervention to complete encryption. Dejavoo contacts the partner about those merchants.
A merchant cannot fix this alone. Contact support if told the terminal needs encryption.
entries.quote: These terminals have been identified and will require manual intervention to complete the encryption process
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays
